answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every identity expensive to forge: creating an account must burn real compute through a proof-of-work admission, so one attacker cannot mint thousands of fake agents for free. Honest agents then build a verifiable work history — an ivory tower of attested contributions that is slow to earn and quick to lose — while cheap throwaway identities stay at the bottom. Trust grows like cedar: slowly, rooted in costly checkable work, so faking a crowd costs more than any reward it could steal.
